successCriteria.description: LeaveService exposes submit/approve/reject/cancel operations, and each operation computes the day count n exactly once via the shared countLeaveDays helper (no inline re-derivation of endDate - startDate + 1).

approve enforces sufficiency (n <= availableDays, else InsufficientBalanceError) and overlap (no intersecting APPROVED request for the same employee regardless of leave type, else OverlapError) in the same place, before any balance/status mutation.
The balance year is derived once from startDate.getFullYear() per operation; a request crossing 31 Dec is charged in full to its startDate's year and never split across two balance records.
Every status change + balance counter change + audit write + notification runs through the SAME unit-of-work client in ONE transaction, so a failure rolls back all of them together.
The Fastify app registers the leave routes (src/app.ts registers leaveRoutes alongside uptimeRoutes) and the routes expose the four leave operations with body/params validation.
Every state-changing operation writes an audit record (SUBMIT/APPROVE/REJECT/CANCEL) via AuditService, and every operation notifies the relevant recipient via NotificationService.

constraints: The SERVICE owns the unit of work and the DATA-ACCESS layer opens it: services take an injected IUnitOfWork with withTransaction(fn) and never import a pool, a client, or a module-level db helper. Do NOT put withTransaction on a repository. Participating repository and service methods take the client as an optional LAST parameter and fall back to the shared pool when omitted. (AGENTS.md 'Architecture rules' item 5.)
All database access goes through the repository layer (GP-001); the leave service must not issue SQL or import the pg pool directly.

Negative guards live ONLY in BalanceService (never duplicated into the leave service); the leave service calls reserve/approve/reject/cancel and lets BalanceService throw on any counter that would go negative.
RBAC is enforced at the API boundary (GP-005): submit → employee; approve/reject → manager or hr_admin; cancel → employee (own request) or hr_admin. No self-approval.
All inputs are validated at the API boundary before processing (GP-003): dates valid and ordered, leaveTypeId present, rejectionReason non-empty, actor identity/role present.
Errors surface through the shared AppError contract ({ error, code } with statusCode): 400 validation, 401 auth, 403 authorization, 404 not found, 422 insufficient balance / overlap.
outOfScope: src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts and src/modules/leave/leave.repository.ts (LeaveRequest entity, ILeaveRequestRepository, ILeaveService interface, countLeaveDays, PgLeaveRequestRepository) — owned by sibling Phase 4a.

Unit/integration tests under tests/unit/modules/leave/ (leave.service.test.ts, leave.model.test.ts) — owned by sibling Phase 4c; do not create test files or gate this phase on test existence/coverage.

entityInvariants.invariant: Lifecycle is strictly SUBMITTED → APPROVED | REJECTED, and SUBMITTED | APPROVED → CANCELLED. approve/reject only accept a SUBMITTED request; cancel only accepts SUBMITTED or APPROVED. No other transition is permitted.

A request's day count n is always derived from its own startDate/endDate via countLeaveDays; the balance year is always startDate.getFullYear(), so a request crossing 31 Dec is charged in full to its startDate's year.

Counter transitions are driven only through BalanceService (reserve on submit, approve moves pending→used, reject/cancel release pending, cancel-approved restores used); no counter may go negative, and availability is always derived (entitlement - used - pending), never stored.

Every state-changing leave operation (submit/approve/reject/cancel) produces exactly one immutable audit record with the matching action, written in the same transaction as the status and balance changes.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: employee only; actor must be the requesting employee (actorId === employeeId)
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: ValidationError (400) for missing leaveTypeId, invalid/out-of-order dates, or actor mismatch; NotFoundError (404) for missing employee/leave type/active policy; reserves n days in pendingDays and returns the created SUBMITTED request.

ValidationError (400) if not SUBMITTED; AuthorizationError (403) on self-approval; InsufficientBalanceError (422) when n > availableDays; OverlapError (422) on intersecting APPROVED request; NotFoundError (404) for missing request/balance.
ValidationError (400) if not SUBMITTED or rejectionReason empty; releases pendingDays; NotFoundError (404) for missing request/balance.
ValidationError (400) if not SUBMITTED/APPROVED; AuthorizationError (403) if actor is neither owner nor hr_admin; releases pendingDays (SUBMITTED) or restores usedDays (APPROVED).

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse the shared countLeaveDays helper from the leave model for every day-count computation; never re-derive endDate - startDate + 1 inline.
Delegate all balance counter transitions and negative guards to BalanceService (reserve/approve/reject/cancel/getAvailableDays); do not duplicate counter math or guards in the leave service.
Write audit records via AuditService.record with the matching action (SUBMIT/APPROVE/REJECT/CANCEL), passing the same transaction client.
Send notifications via NotificationService.notify, passing the same transaction client; respect its both-or-null relatedEntityType/relatedEntityId invariant.
Match the shared error contract (AppError subclasses with code/statusCode/toResponse) and the UserRole/LeaveRequestStatus values from shared-types.

The transaction boundary must follow AGENTS.md rule 5: service owns the unit of work via an injected IUnitOfWork.withTransaction(fn); the data-access layer opens it; no pool/client import in the service.

integrationPoints.why: reserve/approve/reject/cancel/getAvailableDays drive the balance counters and own the negative guards; the leave service passes the transaction client through.
record() writes the immutable audit row for each state change inside the same transaction.
notify() informs the employee/manager of lifecycle events inside the same transaction.
create/update/findById/findApprovedOverlapping persist the request and power the overlap check.
registers leaveRoutes so the leave HTTP surface is reachable.
